decisions.choice: Sign in with DinkusKit.com, per Ship's contract (ship-owner-signin-001 in dinkuskit/ship). DinkusKit.com adds GET /account/ship-sign-in, which checks the signed-in person and sends the browser back to the one fixed address https://ship.dinkuskit.com/auth/callback with a one-time, 60-second, PKCE-bound code. It also adds POST /api/ship-sign-in/token, which trades the code for a 5-minute ship:labels pass (aud dinkus-ship, uid and email) and a rotating refresh token bound to the person's DinkusKit.com sign-in. Owners and Administrators may always print. A plain employee may print once the owner ticks Print shipping labels in Ship (ship:labels). A refresh is refused once the person signs out of DinkusKit.com, their email changes, they are removed or suspended or lose the permission, the business is suspended or unapproved, the operator cuts Ship off, the owner turns Ship off, or an old refresh token comes back. A refresh extends the DinkusKit.com sign-in the way a visit would. The pass carries no store name or reply-to: Commerce sends the EmDash Site title with each order, and Ship keeps its own reply-to setting.

Owners and Administrators may always print. A plain employee may print once the owner ticks Print shipping labels in Ship (ship:labels). A refresh is refused once the person signs out of DinkusKit.com, their email changes, they are removed or suspended or lose the permission, the business is suspended or unapproved, the operator cuts Ship off, the owner turns Ship off, or an old refresh token comes back. decisions.rationale: The Registry has no channels, so only a separate -beta package keeps betas off real stores. A cut-on-demand beta, as OpenClaw cuts betas from a chosen commit, removes the pre-mode enter and exit PRs and a review per beta, and betas exist only when someone is ready to test one. The journeys run on a set-up machine, not in GitHub Actions, so a recorded pass is the gate. Identical files keep the release path the same across plugins. decisions.choice: Release branches, the OpenClaw way. (1) Every change is still a normal PR to main, reviewed by ClawSweeper; main never waits for a beta. (2) Cut beta creates release/X.Y.Z from main at the commit it is pressed on, tags vX.Y.Z-beta.1 there, publishes the -beta package from the branch and presses the journeys. (3) A fix found on beta merges to main through its normal reviewed PR; an 'Add fix to beta' action copies that exact merged commit onto release/X.Y.Z (git cherry-pick -x) and cuts the next beta.N from the branch. A copy that does not apply cleanly stops; nothing reaches a release branch except copies of reviewed main commits and the release bot's version commit. No PR ever targets a release branch, so ClawSweeper (default-branch PRs only) needs no change. (4) Promote, for a beta whose journeys passed, works out the version and changelog on release/X.Y.Z and opens the one 'ci: release vX.Y.Z' PR to main carrying only that version, that changelog section and the removal of the changesets the release consumed. ClawSweeper reviews it and Ronald's merge stays the stable publish yes. On that merge the workflow writes the same version files onto release/X.Y.Z, refuses unless the branch then differs from the beta tag only in the version files, tags vX.Y.Z on the branch, and publishes stable from it. (5) A bug in a released version: the fix merges to main, then is copied onto release/X.Y.(Z+1), made from the vX.Y.Z tag, which cuts X.Y.(Z+1)-beta.1; journeys, then Promote as above. (6) release/* branches accept pushes only from the release GitHub App. Kept from release-beta-cut-071: separate -beta Registry packages, one beta store with every plugin's newest beta, a recorded @running journeys pass naming the beta gates Promote, Cut beta and Promote are pressed on Ronald's word, and every plugin repo runs the same release files with a drift check.

decisions.choice: 1) Each plugin repo (Commerce, Payments, Ship first) keeps its reference article as a docs update file (same format as dinkuskit docs/updates/reference/<plugin>.md), edited in the same PR as the code it describes, so ClawSweeper and Ronald review docs and code together (EmDash practice). 2) ClawSweeper records docs as up to date, missing or not applicable on each plugin PR; missing is a finding to fix before merge, not a hard CI block (OpenClaw practice). 3) Only a stable release publishes: the plugin's release workflow copies the reviewed article at the release tag into dinkuskit docs/updates and pushes it to dinkuskit main with no second review PR; Docs publish then runs as today, keeping its base/_rev guard (an admin edit opens an issue and changes nothing). Main is ahead of the Registry, so nothing publishes on merge. 4) Articles that span plugins (start-here, store-owners/*, developers/*, troubleshooting) stay in dinkuskit, edited there. 5) Version alarm, interim: the twice-monthly Docs publish check compares each article's version_scope with the Registry's latest stable releases and opens one issue per article that is behind. 6) Later checkpoint, not part of this build: benchmark the self-hosted documentation assistant against a subscription model on the same docs-maintenance cases (find stale lines after a release, propose correct replacement text). Goal: a final setup like OpenClaw's, where a docs agent runs daily and keeps every article current; once the chosen agent passes the benchmark and runs daily, the twice-monthly alarm in 5 is retired. The agent's write authority and model choice are decided at that checkpoint.

decisions.choice: 1) Keep Cloudflare Access and the operator allowlist as the only way PEOPLE sign in, and keep the guard's first-Admin and allowlist checks. 2) Agents use EmDash's own API tokens, the way upstream EmDash intends: an Admin creates one token per agent in the EmDash admin with the scopes that agent needs (read-only first, e.g. content:read + mcp:tools; publishing = content:write + menus:manage), and revokes it there. 3) The guard lets a request through without an Access sign-in only when it carries an EmDash token (Bearer ec_pat_ API token or ec_oat_ OAuth access token), only on /_emdash/api/* (REST and /_emdash/api/mcp), never on /_emdash/api/admin/*, setup, auth or oauth, never on a path with empty or dot segments, and only once the CMS has an enabled human Admin. EmDash itself then checks the token, the user's role and the token's scopes (anything unmapped needs the admin scope). 4) Access service tokens stay for existing automation (docs publish) but are no longer the way to connect agents. 5) Cloudflare: /_emdash/api gets an Access Bypass at the edge so token requests reach the worker; the guard and EmDash stay the lock there (an Access cookie still works for the admin UI). 6) Not in this step: a claude.ai OAuth connector (needs the OAuth endpoints reachable without Access; its own decision later). 7) Lands before the next stable release.
